AI is great at summarizing science but poor at explaining when it's unsettled, warns Cato's @dr4liberty. Ask a chatbot if kratom or 7-OH can be dangerous, and it might sound certain — but researchers are still actively debating the question. The fix isn't more government regulation. It's transparency, open debate, and healthy skepticism.

The latest Trustees report sets Social Security's insolvency date to 2032, triggering automatic 22% benefit cuts. Yet Congress just cut program revenue with new tax breaks, threatening younger workers with higher payroll taxes to cover the gap. Delay only raises the cost, explains Cato’s @RominaBoccia.

California hasn’t finished counting primary ballots days after polls closed. Slow results breed distrust and fuel election denialism. Governor Newsom blames election workers, but the real fix is policy: more funding, expanded early voting, and ending late-arriving mail ballots, writes Cato’s @stephen_richer.

posts.text:
Regulation drives up health insurance premiums.

In 2018, Trump freed consumers to buy comprehensive coverage at premiums 60 percent below the lowest-price Obamacare plans. Biden rescinded Trump’s rule. Re-issuing it is not enough. Congress must make relief permanent, argue Cato’s @mfcannon and @dr4liberty.

Check out their policy ideas on how to make health care more affordable in Cato’s Handbook on Affordability: ow.ly/ko2G50Z6Rp3

posts.text:
Laws meant to "protect workers" are actually hurting them. New research shows that the easier it is to switch jobs, the faster wages grow — for everyone, even those who never leave. The most pro-worker policy is the freedom to move, write Cato's @scottlincicome and Chad Smitson.
